correctness.rationale: The proof reduces every white-vertex constraint to the existence of red and blue vertices outside its part. Size-two DST sets are characterized exactly by two singleton parts; explicit size-three and size-four constructions meet the remaining lower bounds. For TDS, each color class must contain an edge, giving the lower bound \(4\), and explicit four-vertex constructions cover every nonstar complete multipartite graph of order at least four. Stars and \(K_3\) are handled separately. Exhaustive definition-level enumeration through order eight found no counterexample.

evidence: The initiating paper proves TDS existence for every connected nonstar graph of order at least four and the lower bound \(\gamma_{\mathrm{tds}}\ge4\), but it does not prove that complete multipartite graphs always attain \(4\).
The same paper characterizes graphs with \(\gamma_{\mathrm{dst}}\) equal to their order and therefore already covers the star branch, but does not imply the complete nonstar \(2/3/4\) classification.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The strongest general theorems were compared by implication. They settle existence, a lower bound, and one extreme DST case; the new constructions and lower bounds are still required for arbitrary multipartite part profiles.

value.rationale: These are newly introduced 2026 domination parameters, and their initiating paper explicitly asks for further bounds and tractable graph classes. Complete multipartite graphs form a canonical test family. The theorem gives a complete arbitrary-part classification, identifies the exact existence boundary for TDS, and shows that every admissible complete multipartite graph attains the universal TDS lower bound. It strictly extends the published \(K_{2,m}\) and complete-graph examples rather than merely recomputing them.
